description.value: A remote beach camp at an exposed coastal bight, reachable only by non-road means; amenities and water are unconfirmed, and conditions will be exposed and self-sufficient.

raw_osm.description: Sheltered from sea swells in all but northeast winds so landing and launching should seldom be a problem. The top of the beach is flat sand and well above most high tides. Reliable stream provides a good fresh water source. Brown bear territory.
raw_osm.name: Open Bight Beach Camp

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record is a backcountry beach campsite (tourism=camp_site, backcountry=yes) on the remote BC coast, accessible only by sea kayak. The Facebook group post by the site admin confirms the location, beach character, and a flowing freshwater stream, closely matching the OSM description text. No formal infrastructure or amenities are mentioned in either source, and the site has no road access.
concerns: No road or trail access — campsite is reachable only by sea kayak or small boat, making it of very limited use to touring cyclists.
OSM description and Facebook post both note brown bear territory; no bear-safe food storage infrastructure is mentioned.
The URL is a Facebook group post (Inside Passage Sea Kayakers), not a dedicated campsite page or land manager website; information may be informal and community-sourced.
No formal address; location is identified only by GPS coordinates (OSM: 51.3661, -127.7694; Facebook post: 51.3663, -127.7699).
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is a real, publicly accessible backcountry campsite confirmed by community posts and matching OSM data. It has no road or trail access and is reached only by sea, limiting practical relevance to touring cyclists, but it is a genuine open site and not excluded by any of the exclusion criteria.
enrichment_extras.notes: A natural freshwater stream is confirmed by both OSM tags ('Reliable stream provides a good fresh water source') and the Facebook post ('A flowing stream provides a good fresh water source'), but potability without treatment is not confirmed.

wow_evidence: reachable only by non-road means; amenities and water are unconfirmed
